newsitem.title: UK: Air cargo trade Feb activity up 0.2pct - Tokyo-Mitsubishi.
newsitem.headline: Air cargo trade Feb activity up 0.2pct - Tokyo-Mitsubishi.

text.p: The index of U.S. air cargo trade activity rose 0.2 percent in February, compared to a 2.3 percent decline in January, the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi said.

In its latest Foreign Trade survey of air freight carriers, seaports and trucking firms released here, the bank quoted one major Asian-based air cargo executive, who noted that the increase in the Japanese consumption tax from three percent to five percent on April 1, accelerated shipping of consumer goods into Japan with the expectatation that they would be sold prior to the higher tax.

Another Asian-based air cargo executive worried that the higher consumption tax ultimately would "adversely affect demand" in Japan and trade with it. A third Asian based air cargo firm said the fact that the Chinese New Year this year was 12 days earlier meant more exports from Asian countries were shifted into January.
The index of future U.S. air cargo business rose to 542.0 in February from 534.4 in January.
The index for air cargo export business rose to 603.4 from 596.7 in January whilst the index of air cargo export expectations rose to 663.0 from 653.9 in January.
Air cargo import business rose to 414.0 from 409.5 in January whilst the import expectations index climbed to 420.0 from 414.8 in January.

The air cargo trade indices are equally weighted composite index of current export of import activity (not seasonally adjusted) with 1989=100. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
